messages:
Nina Chen: Quick RFC follow-up — we should add a lightweight 'annotation' blob to quant profiles so the runtime can make deterministic fast-fallback decisions without loading the whole profile. Thinking small and stable here.
Pieter van der Meer: +1. can you sketch fields? prefer explicit over magic strings.
Nina Chen: Rough sketch below (very small):
```json
{"compat_tags": ["kv-cache-safe", "longctx"], "fallback_priority": ["fp8","int8","4bit"], "quality_budget_pct": "0.5", "telemetry_hint": "degscore_v1"}
```

Samir Patel: love the small blob. question: quality_budget_pct = tolerated relative degrade? how do we measure at runtime?
Nina Chen: yes — it's a contract for ops/telemetry. runtime emits per-request degradation signal (degscore) and we compare against budget to decide fallback. budget is per-profile, per-endpoint overrideable.
Leila Gomez: we need an explicit field for "safety_mode" (eg strict/lenient) so enterprise customers can opt out of aggressive fallbacks. otherwise they will be surprised.
Pieter van der Meer: add a boolean for "enforce_canary_check" too — ensures canary passes before profile becomes default.
Samir Patel: runtime handshake idea: on model load, runtime reads profile.annotation and registers:
- compat_tags => enables/disable optimizations
- fallback_priority => ordered list of fallbacks
- quality_budget_pct => used by on-the-fly triggers

Nina Chen: agree. also suggest storing a tiny fingerprint: "profile_fingerprint" so controller can detect drift when pushing updated profiles.
Leila Gomez: telemetry: we need these signals emitted: 
- profile_fingerprint
- applied_precision
- degscore (float)
- fallback_triggered (tag)
- request_latency (ms)
This will let us correlate quality vs latency/cost.
Pieter van der Meer: how about backward compat? old profiles missing annotation should default to conservative behavior (no automatic fallback). keep safe.
Samir Patel: ops-bot: would it be possible to add a lint that rejects profiles missing mandatory annotation keys when targeting auto-fallback rollout? @ops-bot
ops-bot: lint-rule created: quant-profile:require-annotation-for-autofallback. added as optional in pre-commit hooks. :gear:
Nina Chen: migration plan:
1) land annotation schema & runtime patch that ignores missing annotations (safe default)
2) enable lint and run on existing profiles, flag obvious gaps
3) run a small canary: endpoint-level override to opt-in to auto-fallback
4) collect telemetry for 2 weeks, evaluate degscore distribution, then widen rollout.
Leila Gomez: action: Leila -> write telemetry schema PR, Samir -> runtime annotation reader, Pieter -> lint + deploy check, Nina -> rollout doc. timeline 2 weeks?

Samir Patel: I'll start a runtime PR tomorrow. API sketch for handshake (pseudo):
```yaml
onblocking: true
annotation:
  profile_fingerprint: "sha1:..."
  compat_tags: [kv-cache-safe]
  fallback_priority: [fp8,int8,4bit]
  quality_budget_pct: "0.5"
  safety_mode: "lenient"
```
Pieter van der Meer: I'll open the lint PR and add CI guard that only warns initially.
Nina Chen: sounds good. keep the annotation size tiny (<1KB) so controller-storage/caching unaffected.
Leila Gomez: thumbs up. will post telemetry schema draft in #eng-platform for visibility. :thumbsup:
Samir Patel: one more caveat: for multi-tenant Dedicated customers we should allow per-customer override via endpoint metadata so they can pin behavior.
Nina Chen: agreed — add as explicit override in rollout doc. good catch.
Pieter van der Meer: ok lets sync tomorrow 10am to unblock PRs. :calendar:
Nina Chen: thanks all — short thread. I'll draft the RFC follow-up with the fields and migration steps.
